Tuscany noun

also Tuscan, Etruria

classical

Cic. Div. 1.92 (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. Tuscany (Milton 1674; Tursellinus 1652)
Graesse, Orbis Latinus (1861), index s.v. Toscana: Hetruriae magnus ducatus

Etrūria, Etrūriae f.

noun, first declension

Ancient Etruria, whose name later Latin keeps for Tuscany. Lewis & Short marks the first vowel common. A country takes a preposition: in Etrūriam (to), in Etrūriā (in), ex Etrūriā (from).

Other words

    noun, first declension · also used · late Latin · Eutr. 3.9 (Lewis & Short s.v. Tusci); M-O s.v. Tuscany (Dante; Mercator 1595)

  • Tuscus, Tusca, Tuscum — Tuscan, Etruscan

    declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. Tusci
